literal: An edict asked Hao: "Gai Wu is ninety li north of Chang'an; north of the Wei the land lies empty, grain and fodder are not stocked. We wish to cross south of the Wei and march west—what of it?"
idiomatic: The emperor asked Hao: "Gai Wu lies ninety li north of Chang'an. North of the Wei the country is bare—no grain, no fodder. We mean to cross the Wei and march west. What do you say?"

literal: " Hao said: "Gai Wu's camp is sixty li from here—that is where the rebel chief sits."
idiomatic: " Hao answered: "Gai Wu's camp is sixty li away. That is where the rebel leader sits."

literal: The method for striking a serpent: one must first break the head; when the head is broken, how can the tail stir?"
idiomatic: Strike a serpent: break the head first. Break the head and the tail cannot move."

literal: We ought to seize the moment and strike Gai Wu first."
idiomatic: Take the moment and strike Gai Wu first."

literal: If the army goes now, we reach him in a single day."
idiomatic: March now and we arrive in a day."

literal: After Gai Wu is pacified, we turn back toward Chang'an, and that too is one day's march."
idiomatic: Once Gai Wu is down, we turn back to Chang'an—again one day."

literal: One day's fatigue will not yet do harm."
idiomatic: One day's weariness will not yet harm the men."

literal: In my humble view we should take the northern route."
idiomatic: I would take the northern road."

literal: If we take the southern route, Gai Wu will slowly slip into the northern hills and in the end cannot be pacified."
idiomatic: Take the southern road and Gai Wu will slip into the northern hills at leisure—and never be crushed."

literal: " The emperor would not follow him and crossed south of the Wei.
idiomatic: " The emperor would not listen. He crossed south of the Wei.

literal: Gai Wu heard the emperor had arrived; all scattered into the northern hills—just as Hao had said.
idiomatic: Gai Wu heard the emperor was coming. His men scattered into the northern hills—exactly as Hao had warned.

literal: The army took nothing; the emperor repented of it.
idiomatic: The army won nothing. The emperor repented.

literal: Later, because of Hao's diligence in assisting the Eastern Palace, he was granted one thousand bolts each of silk floss and cloth.
idiomatic: Later, for his service to the crown prince, Hao received a thousand bolts each of floss silk and cloth.

literal: When the emperor hunted in Hexi, he edicted Hao to come to the camp to discuss military affairs.
idiomatic: On a hunt in Hexi the emperor summoned Hao to the camp to discuss military affairs.

literal: Hao memorialized: "Formerly Emperor Wu of Han worried that the Xiongnu were strong and flourishing; therefore he opened the five commanderies of Liangzhou, connected with the Western Regions, spread agriculture and heaped grain, gathering resources to destroy the enemy, striking east and west in alternation."
idiomatic: Hao memorialized: "Han Wudi feared the Xiongnu while they were strong. He opened Liangzhou's five commanderies, reached the Western Regions, farmed and stored grain, and built the means to destroy the foe—striking east and west in turn."

literal: Thus Han had not yet grown weary when the Xiongnu were already spent, and afterward they came to court.
idiomatic: Han had not yet worn itself out when the Xiongnu were spent—and later they came to court.

literal: When Liangzhou was pacified in the past, I in my foolishness thought that while northern rebels were not yet pacified and levies and corvée did not cease, one ought not relocate its people—examining earlier precedents, this was the long-term calculation.
idiomatic: When Liangzhou was pacified I argued, foolishly, that with northern rebels still abroad and levies unceasing, its people should not be moved—that ancient precedent was the far-sighted plan.

literal: If you relocate the people, the land becomes empty; though there are garrison troops, they can only barely guard the frontier.
idiomatic: Move the people and the land goes hollow. Garrisons may remain, but they can only hold the border.

literal: When it comes to a major campaign, military stores are sure to fall short.
idiomatic: For a great campaign, supplies will fail.

literal: Your Majesty, because this matter seemed broad and distant, in the end did not adopt it.
idiomatic: Your Majesty thought the matter too distant and did not adopt it.

literal: As in my foolish opinion, it is still as I urged before: recruit and move wealthy powerful households to fill out the Liang lands.
idiomatic: My view is unchanged: recruit and settle great families to fill the Liang country.

literal: When the armies march, east and west strike together—that is the winning plan."
idiomatic: When armies move, strike east and west together—that is the winning plan."

literal: Hao also submitted the Five Yin Primordial Calendar.
idiomatic: Hao also presented the Five Yin Primordial Calendar.

literal: His memorial said: "In the first year of Emperor Taizong's accession, he charged me to explicate the Rapid Writing Primer, the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, the Odes, the Documents, the Spring and Autumn, the Record of Rites, and the Changes—completed in three years."
idiomatic: His memorial said: "In Taizong's first year I was ordered to master the Rapid Writing Primer, Filial Piety, Analects, Odes, Documents, Spring and Autumn, Rites, and Changes—finished in three years."

literal: He again edicted me to study astronomical stars and calendars, Yi forms, and the Nine Palaces, and there was nothing I did not read through thoroughly.
idiomatic: He again ordered me to study stars, calendars, Yi forms, and the Nine Palaces—I read everything through.

literal: For thirty-nine years, day and night without cease.
idiomatic: For thirty-nine years I did not rest, day or night.

literal: My nature is weak and inferior; my strength does not match a vigorous woman's, and I have no other ability—therefore I devoted mind to books, forgetting sleep and eating.
idiomatic: I am weak by nature—no stronger than a hardy woman—and have no other gift. I gave my mind to books and forgot sleep and food.

literal: Indeed I dreamed of quarreling with ghosts over meaning, and thus obtained the essential arts of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius.
idiomatic: I even dreamed I argued meaning with ghosts—and so came to the essentials of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius.

literal: Then I knew that the ancients had empty and full, that those who spoke falsely were many and those who spoke truly few.
idiomatic: Then I knew the ancients mixed empty with full: false words were many, true words few.

literal: After the First Emperor of Qin burned the books, the classics were cut off and perished.
idiomatic: After Qin Shihuang burned the books, the classics died.

literal: Since Emperor Gao of Han, people in the world who rashly made calendar arts were more than ten households, and none obtained the correctness of Heaven's Way.
idiomatic: Since Han Gaozu more than ten houses rashly made calendars—and none caught Heaven's Way.

literal: Great errors numbered four thousand, small errors were very many, beyond telling.
idiomatic: Great errors ran to four thousand; small errors beyond count.

literal: I pitied that it was so.
idiomatic: I pitied it.

literal: Now, encountering Your Majesty's era of great peace, eliminating falsehood and following truth, the mistaken calendar ought to be reformed to accord with Heaven's Way.
idiomatic: Now, in Your Majesty's peace, casting out falsehood for truth, the false calendar should be corrected to Heaven's Way.

literal: Therefore I earlier memorialized to make a calendar; it is now completed, respectfully submitted.
idiomatic: I memorialized earlier to make a calendar. It is done. I submit it humbly.

literal: I humbly ask Your gracious examination; let my calendar art be displayed to the Erudites of the Central Secretariat, and afterward put into use.
idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to examine it, show my art to the Secretariat erudites, and then put it in use.

literal: Not only people of the time—even Heaven and Earth and ghosts will know I have obtained correctness; the nation's renown for ten thousand generations may surpass the Three August Ones and Five Thearchs."
idiomatic: Not only men of this age—Heaven, Earth, and ghosts will know I have the right measure. The nation's fame for ten thousand generations may surpass the Three August Ones and Five Thearchs."

literal: Hao also, because the various houses of Jin History were largely in error, composed Post-Jin History; it was not finished, but more than fifty scrolls circulated in the world.
idiomatic: Finding the Jin histories mostly wrong, Hao wrote a Post-Jin History. It was unfinished; more than fifty scrolls still circulated.

literal: At the start, Daowu edicted the Secretarial Gentleman Deng Yanhai to compose a National Record of more than ten scrolls, arranging events by year, but the form and example were not fixed; by Mingyuan's time it was abandoned and no longer written.
idiomatic: At first Daowu ordered Deng Yanhai to write a National Record of more than ten scrolls, year by year, but the form was never settled. By Mingyuan the work was abandoned.

literal: In the second year of Shenqi, an edict gathered literary men to compile the national annals.
idiomatic: In Shenqi year two an edict gathered scholars to compile the national annals.

literal: Hao together with his younger brothers Lan and Gao Dan, Deng Ying, Chao Ji, Fan Xiang, Huang Fu, and others jointly participated in the compilation; they narrated and completed the National Record in thirty scrolls.
idiomatic: Hao, his brothers Lan and Gao Dan, Deng Ying, Chao Ji, Fan Xiang, Huang Fu, and others compiled together and finished a thirty-scroll National Record.

literal: The Compiling Clerks Taiyuan Min Kan and Zhao commandery Xi Biao had always flattered and served Hao; they requested to set up stone and inscribe the National Record, to display the straight brush.
idiomatic: Compiling clerks Min Kan of Taiyuan and Xi Biao of Zhao commandery, who had always fawned on Hao, asked to set up stone and inscribe the National Record—to show the straight brush.

literal: They also carved Hao's commentaries on the Five Classics.
idiomatic: They also carved Hao's commentaries on the Five Classics.

literal: Hao agreed to it, and Jingmu approved.
idiomatic: Hao approved; Jingmu was pleased.

literal: They therefore built at three li east of the suburban altar, a plot a hundred paces square; three million work-units were spent before it was done.
idiomatic: They built three li east of the suburban altar on a square plot a hundred paces across—three million work-units before it was finished.

literal: Hao's writing of national affairs was complete but not canonical, yet the stone inscription stood conspicuous on the main road; northerners all deeply harbored resentment and together framed Hao before the emperor.
idiomatic: Hao's account of state affairs was full but not canonical—yet the stone stood plain on the highway. Northerners burned with hate and together denounced him to the emperor.

literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and had the authorities investigate Hao, taking depositions from several hundred Secretarial Gentlemen and long-calendar clerks.
idiomatic: The emperor raged and ordered an inquiry, taking statements from hundreds of secretarial clerks and calendar officers.

literal: Hao confessed to receiving bribes.
idiomatic: Hao confessed to taking bribes.

literal: In the sixth month of the eleventh year of Zhenjun, Hao was executed.
idiomatic: In the sixth month of Zhenjun eleven, Hao was executed.

literal: The Qinghe Cui clan, near and far, together with the Fanyang Lu clan, Taiyuan Guo clan, and Hedong Liu clan—all Hao's affines—had their entire lineages exterminated.
idiomatic: The Qinghe Cui, near and far, with the Fanyang Lu, Taiyuan Guo, and Hedong Liu—all Hao's kin by marriage—were exterminated to the last.

literal: Secretarial clerks, history clerks, and those below—all were put to death.
idiomatic: Secretarial clerks and recorders below them—all were killed.

literal: When Hao was first capped at twenty, Taiyuan Guo Yi gave him his daughter in marriage.
idiomatic: At his capping, twenty, Taiyuan Guo Yi gave him his daughter.

literal: Hao matured late and did not shine with splendor; thus men of the time did not yet know him.
idiomatic: Hao bloomed late and wore no brilliance; men of the time did not yet know him.

literal: Yi's wife was surnamed Wang, elder sister of Song's General of Pacifying the North Wang Zhongde.
idiomatic: Yi's wife Wang was elder sister to Song's General of Pacifying the North Wang Zhongde.

literal: She always marveled at Hao's talent and believed she had gained a worthy son-in-law.
idiomatic: She always marveled at Hao's gifts and thought she had won a true son-in-law.

literal: Before long the daughter died; Dame Wang deeply grieved and wished to give him a younger daughter in second marriage.
idiomatic: Soon the daughter died. Dame Wang grieved deeply and wished to give him a younger daughter in marriage again.

literal: Yi and relatives thought it could not be done, but Dame Wang insisted on giving her to him.
idiomatic: Yi and kin thought it could not be, but Dame Wang insisted.

literal: Yi could not refuse and they renewed the bond of marriage.
idiomatic: Yi could not refuse. The marriage bond was renewed.

literal: Hao was not one who slandered the Buddhist Law, but his wife of the Guo clan revered and loved Buddhist sutras and from time to time recited them.
idiomatic: Hao did not slander the Buddhist Law, but his wife Guo revered the sutras and read them often.

literal: Hao grew angry, took them, and burned them, casting the ashes into the privy.
idiomatic: Hao seized them in anger, burned them, and threw the ashes in the privy.

literal: When Hao was imprisoned in secret, he was placed in a cage and sent to the south of the city; dozens of guards urinated on him; his howling reached the road.
idiomatic: Imprisoned, he was caged and sent south of the city. Dozens of guards urinated on him. His howls reached the road.

literal: Since ministers and grandees suffered disgrace of execution, none had been like Hao; all in the world took it as proof of retribution.
idiomatic: No minister had ever been shamed and killed like Hao. The world called it retribution.

literal: At the start, Hao harmed Li Shun; the foundation and sprouts were already formed. At night he dreamed he set fire to Shun's bedchamber; when the fire rose, Shun died.
idiomatic: When Hao harmed Li Shun the seed was already sown. He dreamed he burned Shun's chamber; the fire rose and Shun died.

literal: Hao and his household stood in a crowd watching.
idiomatic: Hao and his household stood watching.

literal: Before long Shun's younger kinsman came out crying and said: "These men are my enemies!"
idiomatic: Soon Shun's younger kinsman ran out crying: "These are my enemies!"

literal: " He struck them with a spear and cast them all into the river.
idiomatic: " He struck them with a spear and cast them all into the river.

literal: On waking he told his lodging guest Feng Jingren: "This is truly inauspicious."
idiomatic: Waking, he told his guest Feng Jingren: "This is truly ill-omened."

literal: To burn someone with fire is violence at its extreme.
idiomatic: To burn a man is violence at its height.

literal: Moreover, an omen that begins in evil has a final calamity; he who heaps up unkindness has no surplus of blessing.
idiomatic: An omen that starts in evil ends in ruin. He who heaps up wrong has no surplus of blessing.

literal: The steps of ruin are formed; you must take thought for it.
idiomatic: The stair of ruin is built. You must reckon with it.

literal: " Hao said: "I am just thinking about it."
idiomatic: " Hao said: "I am thinking about it."

literal: Yet he could not repent, and at this time his clan was destroyed.
idiomatic: He could not repent—and now his clan was destroyed.

literal: Since Hao was skilled at calligraphy, many people entrusted him to copy the Rapid Writing Primer; from youth to old age he never shrank from labor.
idiomatic: Skilled in calligraphy, many entrusted him with the Rapid Writing Primer. From youth to age he never shirked the work.

literal: What he wrote must have numbered in the hundreds; he always signed "Feng Daiqiang," to show he did not dare transgress the realm.
idiomatic: His copies ran to hundreds. He always signed "Feng Daiqiang"—to show he would not offend the state.

literal: So cautious was he.
idiomatic: Such was his caution.

literal: Hao's calligraphic form and momentum followed his forebears, yet in subtle craft he was not their equal.
idiomatic: Hao's forms followed his forebears; in subtle craft he fell short.

literal: The world treasured his traces; many trimmed, cut, patched, and joined them to serve as models for copying.
idiomatic: The world treasured his traces. Many trimmed and patched them into copy models.

literal: Hao's mother was a granddaughter of Lu Chen.
idiomatic: Hao's mother was Lu Chen's granddaughter.

literal: Hao composed the Preface to the Food Classic: "From my youth to my length of years, what my ears heard and eyes saw—the womanly craft that all my maternal aunts practiced, nothing but brewing and cuisine was not stored in mind."
idiomatic: Hao wrote the Preface to the Food Classic: "From youth to age I saw and heard the woman's work of every aunt—brewing and cuisine, all stored in mind."

literal: Morning and evening they nurtured fathers-in-law and mothers-in-law; in the four seasons they supplied sacrifices—though they had servants, they could not delegate and constantly tended matters with their own hands.
idiomatic: Morning and evening they tended parents-in-law; in the four seasons they made offerings. Though they had servants, they worked with their own hands.

literal: In past years we suffered chaos and rebellion; famine came repeatedly; coarse fare for the mouth could not supply full use of things, and for more than ten years the full array was no longer set out.
idiomatic: In chaos and famine coarse food could not supply the full table. For more than ten years the full spread was not set.

literal: My late mother, fearing long neglect and forgetting, and that the young would have no knowledge of it, and that I in youth did not study books, therefore dictated and taught in nine chapters.
idiomatic: My late mother feared forgetting and that the young would never see it. I had not studied in youth. She dictated nine chapters.

literal: The wording was terse in selection, graceful in forming chapters; keen wit and strong memory—all were of this kind.
idiomatic: The words were terse and graceful; wit and memory were of that kind.

literal: After my parents died, I met the nation's rising dragon's fortune: pacifying violence and removing disorder, extending and fixing the four directions.
idiomatic: After my parents died the realm rose like a dragon—violence pacified, the four quarters fixed.

literal: I filled a position at the highest terrace and participated in great deliberations.
idiomatic: I stood at the highest terrace and joined great counsel.

literal: Rewards were rich and thick; cattle and sheep would have covered a marsh;
idiomatic: Rewards were rich; cattle and sheep might have drowned a marsh;

literal: wealth piled to tens of millions; for clothes, heavy brocade; for food, fine grain and meat.
idiomatic: wealth to tens of millions; clothes heavy brocade; food fine grain and meat.

literal: Looking far back on my whole life, I think of the time when Ji Lu carried rice on his back—a thing that cannot come again.
idiomatic: Looking back on life I think of Ji Lu carrying rice on his back—a time that cannot return.

literal: Therefore I arrange this surviving text to hand down to coming generations."
idiomatic: So I set down this surviving text for generations to come."

literal: Hao's younger brother Jian, styled Zhongliang, also named Lan.
idiomatic: Hao's brother Jian, styled Zhongliang, also called Lan.

literal: He loved learning and in youth was known for fine calligraphy.
idiomatic: He loved learning and was known in youth for fine calligraphy.

literal: In Daowu's early reign he served as Central Secretariat Gentleman, was enfeoffed Marquis of the Fifth Rank, and participated in compiling the National Record.
idiomatic: Under Daowu he was Central Secretariat Gentleman, enfeoffed Fifth-Rank Marquis, and helped compile the National Record.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: Jian's younger brother Tian, styled Shuxuan, childhood name Bai.
idiomatic: Jian's brother Tian, styled Shuxuan, childhood name Bai.

literal: He held the post of Inspector of Yuzhou and was enfeoffed Marquis of Wuyang.
idiomatic: He was Inspector of Yuzhou and Marquis of Wuyang.

literal: Because of Hao he suffered execution by association.
idiomatic: He was executed by association with Hao.

literal: Hong's ancestor Yue, with Fanyang's Lu Chen, were both famed for broad arts.
idiomatic: Hong's ancestor Yue and Fanyang's Lu Chen were famed alike for broad arts.

literal: Chen took Zhong Yao as his model; Yue took Wei Guan; both also studied Su Jing's cursive script, attaining mastery to the full.
idiomatic: Chen followed Zhong Yao; Yue followed Wei Guan. Both studied Su Jing's cursive to the full.

literal: Chen passed to his son Yan; Yan passed to his son Miao;
idiomatic: Chen passed to Yan; Yan to Miao;

literal: Yue passed to his son Qian; Qian passed to his son Hong.
idiomatic: Yue passed to Qian; Qian to Hong.
